'''Tezuka Mitsumori''' (手塚 光盛, ? - [[Juei]] 3rd year (1184)) was a [[bushi]] during the late [[Heian period]]. He was a member of the [[Kanasashi clan]], who served as ritualists of the [[Shimosha]] of the [[Suwa-taisha]]. He was also known as Tezuka Betto's son (or nephew) and had an elder brother, [[Kana Moritomo]]. His common name was Tarō.

In [[The Tale of the Heike]], Mitsumori is identified as a resident of [[Shinano Province]], specifically in the [[Suwa District, Nagano|Suwa District]]. Recent studies suggest that the Tezuka clan, including Mitsumori, was based in the [[Q86729932|Tezuka area]] of [[Ueda, Nagano]] due to the presence of relics such as a residence site, [[Yabusame|yabusame]] structures, a five-story stupa, and temples connected to Mitsumori's legacy.<ref>Ueda City Historical Records (2001), "Manors and Samurai of Ueda," p. 27-31.</ref> However, no descendants of the Tezuka clan currently reside in the area. Tezuka-chō in [[Kaga, Ishikawa]] is named after Tezuka Tarō Mitsumori.

== Career ==
In [[Jishō]] 4th year (1180), when Minamoto no Yoshinaka raised an army, Mitsumori joined as a prominent commander. In [[Juei]] 2nd year (1183), he participated in the [[Battle of Shinohara]]. An episode from this battle is notable in [[The Tale of the Heike]], where Mitsumori defeated [[Sanemori Saitō]].

Sanemori, concealing his old age by dyeing his white hair black, fought valiantly in the colors of the general [[Taira no Koremori]]. After a fierce duel, Mitsumori brought Sanemori's head back to Yoshinaka's camp. When the head was washed, the dye faded, revealing white hair. Recognizing the man as his savior during childhood, Yoshinaka wept openly.<ref>The Tale of the Heike.</ref>

In [[Juei]] 3rd year (1184), during the [[Battle of Awazu]], Mitsumori fought against the armies of [[Minamoto no Noriyori]] and [[Minamoto no Yoshitsune]], dying alongside his lord Yoshinaka. He was one of the last loyal retainers to Yoshinaka.

== Descendants and Legacy ==
Tezuka Mitsumori is associated with several legends and remains:
* His grave is located in [[Q86729932|Tezuka area]], [[Ueda, Nagano]].
* The Tezuka clan changed their surname to Tetsuka and established a memorial for Mitsumori in Osaka's [[Tezukayama]].

Mitsumori's lineage is said to include:
* Tezuka Mitsuharu, a descendant who served as a [[Rangaku|rangaku]] scholar.
* [[Osamu Tezuka]], a famous manga artist, is believed to be a 9th-generation descendant.<ref>Osamu Tezuka's work "Phoenix" ("Civil War Chapter") references his lineage.</ref>
